_doc: M20 exit-refinement coverage matrix — one row per strategy leg. THE milestone's done-condition: every live leg carries a verdict per lever column (shipped / honest_negative / pending / blocked:<reason>). Update in the SAME PR as any verdict-producing work (binding per .claude/skills/exit-refinement). Statuses only from verified evidence (memo/sprint-log/PR refs) — never inferred. ROWS ARE ONE LEG EACH as of 2026-08-09 (BL-20260809-COVERAGE-MATRIX-MULTILEG-ROW-ONE-STATUS): bundled rows carried ONE status for a whole family, so the status described only the leg that passed and the roll-up over-counted `shipped`. Exploded rows carry `exploded_from`. The `shadow fleet` row is deliberately NOT exploded — its label does not enumerate its legs and it is execution:shadow, outside the live-leg done-condition. DO NOT ADD A NEW BUNDLED ROW. ⚠️ EVERY `exit_head_ml` VERDICT IN THIS MATRIX WAS MEASURED UNDER AN ORDER-DEPENDENT TIE-BREAK (BL-20260815-EXIT-HEAD-VERDICT-DEPENDS-ON-LEG-ARGUMENT-ORDER, 2026-08-15). The E1 fold sort is stable and keyed on entry time alone, so trades sharing a bar inherit the order their legs were passed on the command line; on a pooled family every leg entering on the same bar ties. Measured: the same 7 legs in two orders gave identical trade counts, rows and fold shape, yet 8 of 43 folds differed, mean_auc moved up to 0.0331, and two legs lost a usable fold. 27 of the 33 committed rounds are multi-leg `family_pooled` and so exposed; `per_leg` rounds are immune. NO STATUS HERE HAS BEEN RE-GRADED ON THIS — both orders are equally valid and the AUC term is one of four in the gate, so this is a caveat on provenance, NOT a claim that any cell is wrong. `train_exit_head.py --total-sort` fixes it and is DEFAULT-OFF pending an operator-approved re-measure; rounds now stamp `total_sort` so re-measured and legacy rows stay distinguishable.

legend.honest_negative: tested, failed the gate — hard levers/trail stand
legend.shipped_gate_failed: LIVE in config, but a LATER re-sweep failed its gate and the operator chose to HOLD (ref = memo/date). Deliberately distinct from both neighbours: `honest_negative` implies NOT live (recording a live lever there is exactly the bug that made trend_donchian's trail_decay read as a closed negative), and `shipped` asserts 'validated + live' which overclaims once the validation no longer reproduces. A cell here carries a STANDING decision to keep a lever whose justification has lapsed, so it must stay visible in the done-condition roll-up rather than be absorbed into either bucket.

exit_head_ml.ref: E1 RE-RUN 2026-08-13 (relay #8963, fold-mode=trades, fold_blocks fix) — REASON CORRECTED, still blocked. 48 lifetime harness trades; a 50-trade test block needs >=100 for one fold, so BOTH fold modes yield 0. This is a sample-size limit, NOT the calendar-fold defect that blocked the pullback family (now graded). Unblocking needs more trades or a justified lower --min-fold-trades, not a re-run. Years-mode printed '16 candidate folds' here and produced nothing; trades-mode returns 0 and says so. || HORIZON MEASURED 2026-08-13: at 3.60 trades/yr (its 13 OOS trades over the 3.61y since split 2023-01-01 — a MEASURED rate, not a forecast), the 52 trades still needed arrive in about **14.5 YEARS**. `blocked:insufficient_lifetime_trades` reads as a hold that will clear; on this leg it will not clear on any planning horizon. Recorded as a fact on the cell WITHOUT changing its status — whether these become `n/a`, gain a distinct status, or the done-condition changes is a product decision about what M20 'done' means, and it is queued for the operator (BL-20260813-EXIT-HEAD-ML-1D-LEGS-UNREACHABLE). Caveat: the rate assumes the leg keeps trading as observed and stays live; a regime with more signals would shorten it. || ⚠️ THE HORIZON NOTE ABOVE IS WRONG AND IS RETRACTED (2026-08-13, operator challenge: "why aren't we using backtesting? nothing is ever supposed to need live soaking"). It framed the missing trades as arriving through FORWARD LIVE ACCRUAL. They do not. `lifetime harness trades` are produced by a BACKTEST over the built dataset, so the count is governed by HOW MUCH HISTORY WE BUILT, not by elapsed time. `scripts/ops/build_trainer_datasets.sh:925` sets `EQ_1D_START="${EQ_1D_START:-2015-01-01}"` and every equity 1d dataset is built from that date via yfinance — a CHOSEN window (~11.6y), not a limit of the available data. yfinance serves SPY from 1993, QQQ from 1999, IWM from 2000, SPLG from 2005, SCHA/TQQQ/QLD from 2009-2010. So this cell is blocked by a configuration default, and the remedy is a dataset rebuild over a longer window rather than a milestone decision or a wait. The arithmetic in the retracted note is still valid as a TRADES-PER-YEAR-OF-DATA rate — only the forward-in-time interpretation was wrong. NOT YET MEASURED: the actual span of the built files (trainer relay #9049 pending) and how many trades a longer window really yields, since the earlier-regime trade rate need not match the recent one. See BL-20260813-EXIT-HEAD-ML-1D-LEGS-UNREACHABLE. || ⚠️ SECOND CORRECTION, 2026-08-13, and it supersedes the EQ_1D_START note above on TWO points. (a) THE FILES DO NOT START AT 2015. Measured on the trainer (relay #9049): SPY_1d 2010-01-04..2026-07-07, 4152 rows. So EQ_1D_START's 2015-01-01 default is NOT what built these; field beats comment, and my '~11.6y chosen window' was wrong. (b) THE BAR IS 3x THE BLOCK, NOT 2x. `fold_blocks` yields u = floor(N/b) - 1 usable folds and `per_leg_summary` requires u >= 2, so a leg needs N >= 3b = **150** trades at block 50 — not the 100 this ref and every sibling states. At exactly 100 a leg gets ONE fold and the gate rejects it on `u >= 2`. CONSEQUENCE: extending to full inception does NOT rescue this leg — projecting the leg's own measured trades/yr over the extra history gives about 97 (from 1993) lifetime trades against the 150 needed, and ZERO of the seven equity legs reach it. So the data window is not the binding constraint after all; the BLOCK SIZE is, which is why it is being derived rather than assumed (operator decision 2026-08-13). Pending: relay #9055 measures the per-trade dispersion the derivation needs. Nothing here changes this cell's status. || ✅ BLOCK SIZE DERIVED 2026-08-13 — this cell's blocker is now understood and it is NOT an arbitrary number. docs/research/M20-E1-block-size-derivation-2026-08-13.md, measured over 21 e1_report.json / 262 folds / 15 groups: sigma_d ~0.747R, standardized effect delta ~0.105 (5 of 15 groups NEGATIVE). b=(z_p/delta)^2 puts the 0.75-0.80 per-fold reliability band at 41-64 trades and b=50 gives 0.771 — so 50 STAYS. Crucially the derivation also closes the route this cell invites: modelling the whole gate (>=2/3 of u folds, u=floor(N/b)-1) shows P_detect is NOT monotonic in b, and every apparent optimum sits at a u where 2/3 is cheap to hit by luck (50% single-condition false-positive rate), so tuning b to unblock legs would select the settings easiest to pass BY CHANCE. AT THIS LEG'S LIFETIME NO BLOCK SIZE YIELDS A TRUSTWORTHY VERDICT — at N=98 the only gradeable options give either 0.49 power or a 50% FP rate. The honest disposition is therefore NOT 'wait for trades' and NOT 'lower the block'; it is that the exit head's edge (delta ~0.105, inconsistent across families) is too small to grade on a leg this size. That upstream question is the open one. || ⚠️ A CALENDAR-GEOMETRY VERDICT EXISTS FOR THIS LEG AND WE ARE DELIBERATELY NOT GRADING FROM IT (added 2026-08-14; audited in PR #9099, numbers re-verified from the report via trainer relays #9112 + #9113, each with a positive control). `eh_1d_pooled/allmix/e1_report.json` carries `per_leg['spy_trend_long_1d']` = **honest_negative** (oos_trades 29, usable_folds 9, beats_actual 4/9, beats_hard 3/9, floor 25). THE `blocked:` STATUS ABOVE IS STILL CORRECT — the previous ref simply never said this choice had been made, so the next auditor finds a 'not enough trades' cell beside a verdict and reasonably reads the matrix as STALE. WHY WE DECLINE: that report is `fold_mode: None` / `min_fold_trades: None` — the LEGACY CALENDAR cut, not the trades geometry whose 50-trade block this cell's block reason is stated against — and `train_exit_head`'s own `per_leg_note` says the family-pooled block is 'the right unit to TRAIN on and the wrong one to record a verdict from'. Grading a trades-geometry cell from a calendar-geometry verdict would be exactly the incomparable-evidence error that note exists to prevent. AND THESE ARE THE WEAKEST VERDICTS IN THE PROGRAMME: per the block-size derivation § 6, `allmix` votes per LEG on the leg's own trades while blocks are cut over the FAMILY's pooled trades, so its median n_leg is **5** (min 1) — a `candidate` here is a near-coin-flip majority over 9 folds of ~5 trades each, and anyone re-grading from it would be promoting the thinnest evidence we have. INTERNAL CHECK that these verdicts are at least self-consistent: the only two legs graded `insufficient_base` are exactly the two whose oos_trades fall under the floor of 25 (qld 23, tqqq 24). Basis: docs/research/M20-E1-block-size-derivation-2026-08-13.md § 6.

exit_head_ml.ref: E1 RE-RUN 2026-08-13 (relay #8963, fold-mode=trades, fold_blocks fix) — REASON CORRECTED, still blocked. 65 lifetime harness trades; a 50-trade test block needs >=100 for one fold, so BOTH fold modes yield 0. This is a sample-size limit, NOT the calendar-fold defect that blocked the pullback family (now graded). Unblocking needs more trades or a justified lower --min-fold-trades, not a re-run. Years-mode printed '16 candidate folds' here and produced nothing; trades-mode returns 0 and says so. || HORIZON MEASURED 2026-08-13: at 4.43 trades/yr (its 16 OOS trades over the 3.61y since split 2023-01-01 — a MEASURED rate, not a forecast), the 35 trades still needed arrive in about **7.9 YEARS**. `blocked:insufficient_lifetime_trades` reads as a hold that will clear; on this leg it will not clear on any planning horizon. Recorded as a fact on the cell WITHOUT changing its status — whether these become `n/a`, gain a distinct status, or the done-condition changes is a product decision about what M20 'done' means, and it is queued for the operator (BL-20260813-EXIT-HEAD-ML-1D-LEGS-UNREACHABLE). Caveat: the rate assumes the leg keeps trading as observed and stays live; a regime with more signals would shorten it. || ⚠️ THE HORIZON NOTE ABOVE IS WRONG AND IS RETRACTED (2026-08-13, operator challenge: "why aren't we using backtesting? nothing is ever supposed to need live soaking"). It framed the missing trades as arriving through FORWARD LIVE ACCRUAL. They do not. `lifetime harness trades` are produced by a BACKTEST over the built dataset, so the count is governed by HOW MUCH HISTORY WE BUILT, not by elapsed time. `scripts/ops/build_trainer_datasets.sh:925` sets `EQ_1D_START="${EQ_1D_START:-2015-01-01}"` and every equity 1d dataset is built from that date via yfinance — a CHOSEN window (~11.6y), not a limit of the available data. yfinance serves SPY from 1993, QQQ from 1999, IWM from 2000, SPLG from 2005, SCHA/TQQQ/QLD from 2009-2010. So this cell is blocked by a configuration default, and the remedy is a dataset rebuild over a longer window rather than a milestone decision or a wait. The arithmetic in the retracted note is still valid as a TRADES-PER-YEAR-OF-DATA rate — only the forward-in-time interpretation was wrong. NOT YET MEASURED: the actual span of the built files (trainer relay #9049 pending) and how many trades a longer window really yields, since the earlier-regime trade rate need not match the recent one. See BL-20260813-EXIT-HEAD-ML-1D-LEGS-UNREACHABLE. || ⚠️ SECOND CORRECTION, 2026-08-13, and it supersedes the EQ_1D_START note above on TWO points. (a) THE FILES DO NOT START AT 2015. Measured on the trainer (relay #9049): IWM_1d 2010-01-04..2026-07-07, 4152 rows. So EQ_1D_START's 2015-01-01 default is NOT what built these; field beats comment, and my '~11.6y chosen window' was wrong. (b) THE BAR IS 3x THE BLOCK, NOT 2x. `fold_blocks` yields u = floor(N/b) - 1 usable folds and `per_leg_summary` requires u >= 2, so a leg needs N >= 3b = **150** trades at block 50 — not the 100 this ref and every sibling states. At exactly 100 a leg gets ONE fold and the gate rejects it on `u >= 2`. CONSEQUENCE: extending to full inception does NOT rescue this leg — projecting the leg's own measured trades/yr over the extra history gives about 104 (from 2000) lifetime trades against the 150 needed, and ZERO of the seven equity legs reach it. So the data window is not the binding constraint after all; the BLOCK SIZE is, which is why it is being derived rather than assumed (operator decision 2026-08-13). Pending: relay #9055 measures the per-trade dispersion the derivation needs. Nothing here changes this cell's status. || ✅ BLOCK SIZE DERIVED 2026-08-13 — this cell's blocker is now understood and it is NOT an arbitrary number. docs/research/M20-E1-block-size-derivation-2026-08-13.md, measured over 21 e1_report.json / 262 folds / 15 groups: sigma_d ~0.747R, standardized effect delta ~0.105 (5 of 15 groups NEGATIVE). b=(z_p/delta)^2 puts the 0.75-0.80 per-fold reliability band at 41-64 trades and b=50 gives 0.771 — so 50 STAYS. Crucially the derivation also closes the route this cell invites: modelling the whole gate (>=2/3 of u folds, u=floor(N/b)-1) shows P_detect is NOT monotonic in b, and every apparent optimum sits at a u where 2/3 is cheap to hit by luck (50% single-condition false-positive rate), so tuning b to unblock legs would select the settings easiest to pass BY CHANCE. AT THIS LEG'S LIFETIME NO BLOCK SIZE YIELDS A TRUSTWORTHY VERDICT — at N=98 the only gradeable options give either 0.49 power or a 50% FP rate. The honest disposition is therefore NOT 'wait for trades' and NOT 'lower the block'; it is that the exit head's edge (delta ~0.105, inconsistent across families) is too small to grade on a leg this size. That upstream question is the open one. || ⚠️ A CALENDAR-GEOMETRY VERDICT EXISTS FOR THIS LEG AND WE ARE DELIBERATELY NOT GRADING FROM IT (added 2026-08-14; audited in PR #9099, numbers re-verified from the report via trainer relays #9112 + #9113, each with a positive control). `eh_1d_pooled/allmix/e1_report.json` carries `per_leg['iwm_trend_long_1d']` = **candidate** (oos_trades 42, usable_folds 9, beats_actual 7/9, beats_hard 7/9, floor 25). THE `blocked:` STATUS ABOVE IS STILL CORRECT — the previous ref simply never said this choice had been made, so the next auditor finds a 'not enough trades' cell beside a verdict and reasonably reads the matrix as STALE. WHY WE DECLINE: that report is `fold_mode: None` / `min_fold_trades: None` — the LEGACY CALENDAR cut, not the trades geometry whose 50-trade block this cell's block reason is stated against — and `train_exit_head`'s own `per_leg_note` says the family-pooled block is 'the right unit to TRAIN on and the wrong one to record a verdict from'. Grading a trades-geometry cell from a calendar-geometry verdict would be exactly the incomparable-evidence error that note exists to prevent. AND THESE ARE THE WEAKEST VERDICTS IN THE PROGRAMME: per the block-size derivation § 6, `allmix` votes per LEG on the leg's own trades while blocks are cut over the FAMILY's pooled trades, so its median n_leg is **5** (min 1) — a `candidate` here is a near-coin-flip majority over 9 folds of ~5 trades each, and anyone re-grading from it would be promoting the thinnest evidence we have. INTERNAL CHECK that these verdicts are at least self-consistent: the only two legs graded `insufficient_base` are exactly the two whose oos_trades fall under the floor of 25 (qld 23, tqqq 24). Basis: docs/research/M20-E1-block-size-derivation-2026-08-13.md § 6.

So the ⚠️ caveat above no longer gates this cell's conclusion — it is kept as the record of how the first verdict was obtained.

(1) "alone this leg clears ZERO folds" is NO LONGER TRUE and must not be re-quoted: under trade-blocking (`fold_mode=trades`, `min_fold_trades=50`) this leg alone clears 5 usable fold(s) of 50 trades each. Pooling was a workaround for calendar-year folds, not a property of the leg.
(2) THE POOLED RUN'S PER-LEG NUMBERS FLATTERED BOTH LEGS. Read off a model trained on BOTH legs' rows, this leg scored beats_actual=4/7 beats_hard=2/7 auc=0.5791; trained on its own rows it scores 1/5, 1/5, auc=0.5452. READ IT AS A DIRECTION, NOT A PAIRED TEST: the two runs cut different partitions (7 calendar folds vs 5 trade blocks) over different n (249 vs 250), so no single fold is comparable across them. The usable claim is that a per-leg verdict attributed out of a POOLED model is not the same measurement as one trained per leg, and here it was the more generous of the two — a caution for any future pooled attribution, not just this cell.

exit_head_ml.ref:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 (relay #8921) — n_oos=168, auc=0.5496, beats_actual=6/7, beats_hard=5/7 -> honest_negative. FIRST exit_head_ml verdict for any trend-side leg. Two enabling fixes: #8901 made the rows exist at all (this harness emitted no exit_time/entry/sl, so 100% were dropped), and POOLING made them gradeable — alone this leg clears ZERO folds (all 11-38 trades vs --min-fold-trades 50); pooled with its sibling, 504 trades / 12075 rows give 7 of 9 usable folds (2019-2025; 2018 missed at test=49, one trade short, and 2026 at 23).

⚠️ HOW THIS WAS PRODUCED, because the shipped pipeline does NOT do it: the two legs' rows.jsonl were CONCATENATED BY HAND into one family dir and trained once. Rows are byte-identical to what each leg trained on alone (cat only, no transformation), so the pooling is the single isolated variable. `family_of()` still gives each leg its own dir, so a re-run of the standard round reproduces `folds=0`, NOT this verdict — see BL-20260813-FAMILY-RESOLVER-DRIFT-SCALP-NEVER-POOLED, whose operator decision this experiment exists to inform.

Attribution verified, not assumed: the pooled rows still carry their own `strategy` (7030 slv / 5045 uso) and per_leg_summary cut a separate verdict with its own denominator for each. live_trades=0 for both, so the E1->E2 live arm is unevaluated — which bars a PASS but not a negative: the harness arm failed on its own.

=== RE-MEASURED 2026-08-16 (relay #9532/#9533), PER LEG ON THE SHIPPED PIPELINE — n_oos=150, 3 usable fold(s), beats_actual=1/3, beats_hard=1/3, mean_auc=0.5421 -> honest_negative. THE VERDICT IS UNCHANGED AND NOW RESTS ON A RUN THE PIPELINE CAN REPRODUCE: no hand concatenation, one model per leg, `m20_exit_head_round.py --legs slv_trend_1h,uso_trend_1h --tf 1h`. So the ⚠️ caveat above no longer gates this cell's conclusion — it is kept as the record of how the first verdict was obtained.

⚠️ TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE TEXT ABOVE, both measured, not inferred.
(1) "alone this leg clears ZERO folds" is NO LONGER TRUE and must not be re-quoted: under trade-blocking (`fold_mode=trades`, `min_fold_trades=50`) this leg alone clears 3 usable fold(s) of 50 trades each. Pooling was a workaround for calendar-year folds, not a property of the leg.
(2) THE POOLED RUN'S PER-LEG NUMBERS FLATTERED BOTH LEGS. Read off a model trained on BOTH legs' rows, this leg scored beats_actual=6/7 beats_hard=5/7 auc=0.5496; trained on its own rows it scores 1/3, 1/3, auc=0.5421. Both legs moved the same way (slv 4/7→1/5, uso 6/7→1/3), which is why it is worth stating at all. READ IT AS A DIRECTION, NOT A PAIRED TEST: the two runs cut different partitions (7 calendar folds vs 3 trade blocks) over different n (168 vs 150), so no single fold is comparable across them. The usable claim is that a per-leg verdict attributed out of a POOLED model is not the same measurement as one trained per leg, and here it was the more generous of the two — a caution for any future pooled attribution, not just this cell.

tp_geometry_legend._field: tp_geometry — WHICH TAKE-PROFIT GEOMETRY a cell's verdict was measured under. Set per CELL (inside a lever column), never per row: one leg can carry a live-parity re-sweep on one lever and pre-cutover evidence on another. tp_geometry_legend._why_it_exists: BL-20260810-BACKTEST-DOES-NOT-MODEL-THE-LIVE-CAPPED-TP: production clamps the take-profit to ~9.9% from entry while the harnesses modelled NO take-profit, so a verdict measured before that fix describes a book production does not run. This field says which geometry produced a verdict. That is its whole job.
tp_geometry_legend.live_parity: measured WITH the live TP clamp applied — the book that actually trades.
tp_geometry_legend.no_take_profit: measured on a book with NO take-profit: the pre-2026-08-10 harness default, and still the default for any driver that does not pass --tp-cap-pct. A verdict here rests on a book production does not run, and a DATE CANNOT CLEAR IT — a cell re-swept after the cutover but still built without the cap is stale on geometry, not on age.
tp_geometry_legend.ABSENT_means_unrecorded: ⚠️ A MISSING tp_geometry MEANS 'WE DID NOT LOOK', NOT 'presumably fine'. Absence collapses three different conditions — (a) measured at live parity and nobody stamped it, (b) measured on the pre-cutover no-TP default, which is the DEFAULT EXPECTATION for anything dated before the cutover, and (c) nobody looked. The reassuring reading is the one that is wrong for most of the population. The roll-up counts these as `unrecorded` and reports the fraction rather than listing marked cells, so completeness is never inferred from the cells that happen to carry a value.
tp_geometry_legend._coverage_2026_08_16: 170 of 416 cells (40.9%) carry a value: live_parity 167, no_take_profit 3, absent 246. Measured directly off this file. The roll-up's own figure is over the LIVE-leg population (a different, smaller denominator) — both are correct and neither is the other.
tp_geometry_legend._remaining_work: Stamping the 246 absent cells is NOT done here and must not be guessed from dates: BL-20260814-TP-GEOMETRY-RECORDED-ON-2-PERCENT-OF-CELLS-SO-ABSENCE-CANNOT-MEAN-ANYTHING criterion (2) requires each cell's own `ref` to establish live_parity or no_take_profit, with `unrecorded` stamped only where the ref establishes neither. A date is a proxy, and that row exists because a proxy was trusted.
tp_geometry_legend._unstamped_ceiling_note: 234 -> 229 on 2026-08-24, and the REASON matters more than the number. The ceiling is an ABSOLUTE count of unstamped LIVE cells, and the live population shrank: slv_trend_1h was demoted live -> shadow (Tier-3, operator-approved), taking its 9 lever cells — 5 of them unstamped — out of the `live_only` denominator. The ratchet had been EXACTLY tight at 234; leaving it there would have left 5 cells of slack in which a live cell could silently lose its tp_geometry stamp with the guard still green. This file's own docstring names raising the ceiling as the cheap lie the guard exists to resist — a demote produces the identical loosening while looking innocent, which is why it is corrected here in a diff rather than absorbed. Verified by the planted-omission self-tests in tests/test_m20_tp_geometry_guard.py, which FAILED at 234 (deleting a stamp gave 230, under the stale ceiling) and pass at 229.

legend_bracket_geometry: bracket_geometry is the ENTRY BRACKET TRIPLE (tp_at_r x atr_stop_mult x timeout_bars) — a new DIMENSION, not a ninth lever. The eight lever columns beside it are all POST-ENTRY OVERRIDES on a bracket fixed at entry; this column grades that bracket itself. Added 2026-08-20 closing BL-20260820-TP-LEVEL-IS-THE-ONE-EXIT-PARAMETER-NEVER-SWEPT. Graded NET OF FEES, unlike the fee-free R basis the lever columns use, because a lower target raises turnover and a fee-free comparison would flatter it exactly where it is most likely to pass.

known_caveats._doc: Defects filed against the tools that PRODUCED this matrix, adjudicated so a reader of any cell can see what conditions it. Written 2026-08-27 on operator direction after an audit found ~50 open backlog rows naming a producing tool of this file and NOT ONE visible in it (RESEARCH-INFRA-AUDIT-2026-08-27.md section 8.4: 'a defect filed against a PRODUCER does not reach the ARTIFACTS it already produced'). Enforced by scripts/ci/check_artifact_caveats.py: every OPEN row naming a producer must sit in exactly one bucket, a dismissal must state a reason, and pending_adjudication is RATCHETED so the debt can only shrink.
known_caveats._how_to_read: conditions_verdicts = a reader of ANY cell must see this. reviewed_not_conditioning = looked at, does not condition the verdicts, reason stated. pending_adjudication = not yet judged (honest, and capped by pending_baseline). This block does NOT assert the caveats are correct - it asserts the judgement was MADE and is visible.
known_caveats._headline: The broadest caveat is the power one: over the 113 cells that state a base count the MEDIAN OOS base is 33 trades and 94.7% are under 50. Base size does not separate pass from fail fleet-wide, so this conditions the WHOLE matrix rather than distinguishable cells - which is why there is no per-cell `underpowered` status. Neither the 329 honest_negative verdicts nor the 22 passed_unshipped are safe to read as settled without checking the rows below.
